text_post: This is very good although also somewhat irrelevant. A three line whip in literal terms is a written notice, underlined three times to denote urgency, to members of a political party to attend a parliamentary vote. In more practical terms it means the MP attends the vote and votes in accordance with the party line unless they are physically unable to do so (out of country for example) those voting against the party line face party disciplinary measures and those on the front benches (ministers/shadow ministers) can expect to lose their positions. Corbyn for all else he may be is no idiot, he knows if his party attempts to stop this they will never see power again. The vote was sold to the electorate as a straight choice, leave or remain with the voters decision being final. They chose by 52-48%, (a popular majority of 1.3 million votes) to leave, a little over 2/3 of the voting regions voted leave and various analysis estimate that a similar breakdown applies at the constituency level. Essentially the same vote repeated at a general election would see UKIP forming a government with over 400 seats, for reference the last such majority outside of wartime occurred in 1931. It would political suicide for any MP or party to attempt to halt the process at this point.
